property_summary: The Put function should always be non-reentrant (locked during execution), but the bug removes the modifier, allowing a re-entrant caller to call Collect within Put and violate the balance invariant that the contract's ETH balance equals the sum of all Acc balances.

After any call to Put, the contract should be locked during execution (reentrancy guard engaged), so a reentrant caller cannot re-enter via Collect; the bug removes the modifier, allowing reentry that empties ETH while leaving internal balance unchanged.

After a call to Put, the nonReentrant_ lock must always be released (locked_ equals false); the bug removes the modifier, so a re-entrant call to Put via the fallback function can cause Put to be entered while locked_ is still true, leaving the lock permanently set.

After any successful call to Put, the internal balance of the caller must increase by at least msg.value; the bug removes the nonReentrant_ modifier from Put, allowing a re-entrant caller to call Collect within Put, which can reduce the balance and violate the invariant.

After a re-entrant call pattern where a caller re-enters C during Put, the internal balance of the caller recorded in Acc must equal the sum of all deposits minus withdrawals; the bug removes the nonReentrant_ modifier, allowing a re-entrant call to Collect within Put that drains ETH without updating the internal balance, violating the invariant.
For any payable call to Put, the caller's Acc balance must increase by at least the sent msg.value; the mutant adds zero, so the balance fails to increase.
After any call to Put(...) with a value, the caller's Acc balance must increase by at least msg.value; the mutant adds zero so the balance does not reflect the sent Ether.

After a successful Put call, the contract's ether balance must increase by at least msg.value; the buggy version adds zero but still emits msg.value in the log, allowing the invariant to be broken by sending value that is not credited to any user's balance.

After any call to Put with a nonzero value, the contract's ETH balance must increase by the sent amount; the mutant adds zero to the user's balance but the contract still receives the Ether, causing a discrepancy.

After a successful Put(N) with value V, sum of all Acc balances of all addresses ever used must equal the contract's ether balance minus any prior successful Collect withdrawals; the mutant adds zero to the caller's balance yet the contract still receives V, breaking the equality.
After a Put call, the sender's balance in the Acc mapping exactly equals the cumulative Ether they have sent; the mutant fails to add msg.value, so the balance remains lower than the total sent.
The sum of all Acc balances equals the contract's own Ether balance for any sequence of Put calls, but the mutant fails to credit balances, breaking this invariant.

After any number of Put calls from any actors with any amounts, the sum of balances over all Acc entries equals address(c).balance for the reference, but the mutant fails to add msg.value to balances, so the sum eventually becomes strictly less than the contract's Ether balance.

After any sequence of Put calls, the sum of unlock times recorded across all holders equals the number of Put calls for the reference; the mutant still increments unlock times but fails to credit balances, so the sum of unlock times (or number of entries) remains equal, which does not distinguish the bug. Therefore, for the reference, the contract's Ether balance exactly equals the sum of all Acc[actor].balance + any external transfers; the mutant fails to add msg.value to balances, so the sum of balances becomes strictly less than the contract's Ether balance after at least one Put with a non-zero amount.

After a single Put call with any non-zero amount, the reference contract correctly records the sender's balance exactly equal to the sent amount, while the mutant omits the balance update, making the balance zero.
After a call to Put(u), the unlockTime stored in Acc[msg.sender] must equal max(u, block.timestamp); the mutant always sets it to block.timestamp, violating this invariant when u > block.timestamp.

After a call to Put(u), if u > block.timestamp then Collect reverts because unlockTime must be > block.timestamp to allow collection; the mutant sets unlockTime = block.timestamp so Collect succeeds immediately, violating the invariant that Collect reverts when u > block.timestamp (i.e. funds are locked until u).
After Put(u) with u > block.timestamp, the unlockTime in Acc must be >= u; the mutant sets it to block.timestamp, violating this lower bound.
After Put(u), if u > block.timestamp then unlockTime must be strictly greater than block.timestamp; the mutant sets it to block.timestamp, so the invariant unlockTime > block.timestamp is violated.

For any initial unlock time u, after calling Put(u), the value of Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime must equal block.timestamp if u <= block.timestamp, and must equal u if u > block.timestamp; the mutant always sets it to block.timestamp, violating the rule when u > block.timestamp.

The sum of all balances in Acc must equal the contract's Ether balance, and after any number of Put calls, a user's balance must be at least the total value they have sent. The mutant overwrites the balance with msg.value instead of adding it, so after any second Put call to the same address, the user's balance equals only the last msg.value, not the cumulative sum.

After at least two `Put` calls by the same address, the caller's `Acc[caller].balance` must be strictly greater than the value sent in the last call (because previous contributions remain). The mutant overwrites instead of adding, so `Acc[caller].balance` equals only the last sent value.

After any number of Put calls by the same address, the caller's balance in Acc must equal the total sum of all msg.value they have ever sent, not just the last one; the mutant sets the balance to msg.value, losing prior contributions.

After two successive Put calls by the same caller, the caller's Acc balance must be at least the sum of the two msg.values; the mutant sets the balance to only the second msg.value, breaking the inequality.
After any Put call, unlockTime must be at least block.timestamp. The mutant omits updating unlockTime, so it can remain zero even when block.timestamp > 0, violating this invariant.
After a Put call that sets _unlockTime > block.timestamp, the account's unlockTime must equal _unlockTime, but the buggy version leaves it unchanged (e.g., 0), violating this equality.

After a non-zero Put call, the account's unlockTime must be strictly greater than 0; the buggy version omits the update, leaving unlockTime at its initial value of 0, violating this lower-bound invariant.

After a Put call with _unlockTime set to a future timestamp, the account's unlockTime must be at least that future timestamp, but the mutant leaves unlockTime unchanged, so a subsequent check can show it is less than the intended _unlockTime when _unlockTime is in the future.

After any successful Put call with _unlockTime greater than block.timestamp, the account's unlockTime must be strictly greater than block.timestamp; the mutant omits the storage update, so the invariant fails when _unlockTime was set to a future timestamp but unlockTime remains zero or an old past timestamp.

After a successful call to Put, the nonReentrant_ lock must be reset to false. The buggy modifier permanently locks the contract, so a second call to Put reverts, while the reference contract allows repeated calls.
After a successful Put, the contract must remain callable again (not permanently locked). The buggy modifier never releases the lock, so a second call reverts—the reference allows repeated calls.

A successful Put call must always enable a subsequent non-zero Collect (if balance/time conditions are met); the buggy modifier permanently locks the contract, causing the subsequent Collect to revert.
After any sequence of Put calls, the contract's locked_ flag must be false; the buggy modifier never resets it, so after the first call it remains true.

After two consecutive Put calls from the same sender with sufficient ETH to cover both and no other interactions, the reference contract's Acc[msg.sender].balance equals the sum of the two amounts sent; the buggy contract reverts on the second call, preventing the second deposit.
If a Collect call succeeds without reverting, the contract balance must decrease by exactly the amount collected.
A successful Collect must not permit any reentrant call to C.
A Collect call that does not revert must never be able to make a second Collect call succeed without reverting.
A Collect call that succeeds must have been invoked while locked_ was false (i.e., no reentrant call was in progress).
A Collect call that succeeds without reverting must cause the next identical Collect call to revert.
